key_concepts: Mixtures consist of two or more substances physically combined and may vary in composition
Each substance in a mixture retains its own chemical identity
Homogeneous mixtures have evenly distributed particles and uniform appearance
Heterogeneous mixtures have more than one observable phase and can be separated physically
Pure substances include elements and compounds
Water is a pure substance because its molecules are identical
Mixtures are classified by particle size as solutions, suspensions, and colloids
Suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures with solid particles large enough for sedimentation
Colloids have particles of colloidal dimension distributed in a dispersion medium
Colloids exhibit the Tyndall effect when a light beam passes through
